reason: The hypothesis claims that Co removal increases SFE and promotes twinning, but the cited evidence (E3) shows a Co-containing alloy with high SFE deforming by dislocation glide, and E1 shows a Co-containing alloy with negative SFE exhibiting twinning, which contradicts the proposed SFE-twinning relationship. No cited evidence directly supports the key premise that Co removal increases SFE or that higher SFE promotes twinning over slip.
premises: Removing Co from CoCrFeMnNi increases the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the FeNiCrMn alloy.
Increased SFE shifts the deformation mechanism from dislocation slip to mechanical twinning.
The slip-to-twinning transition occurs over specific temperature and strain-rate regimes.
The transition causes anomalous changes in strain-hardening and yield strength relative to the Co-containing alloy.
The Co-containing baseline alloy exhibits predominantly dislocation slip with lower twin density under the test conditions.
